$comment: HARNESS-16 — the AI-review engine registry (PRD §3 ports doctrine applied to CI).
The review PORT is fixed and engine-agnostic: read a CODEOWNERS-protected reviewer
definition, diff the PR against its base, write a review whose last line is a
`VERDICT:` line. Every ADAPTER (engine) must satisfy exactly that contract, and the
verdict parse in ai-review.yml is the contract test that binds all of them equally —
an engine that cannot produce a parseable verdict fails as DID NOT COMPLETE rather
than being silently accepted.
Swapping or adding an engine is a CONFIG change here plus one guarded adapter step in
.github/workflows/ai-review.yml. scripts/ai-review-matrix.mjs refuses to build a
matrix for an enabled engine that has no adapter, so a half-added engine fails loudly
instead of silently producing no review.
This file is deliberately NOT overridable by a repository variable. Under HG-0006 the
reviewer prompts and the model serving them are model configuration, and HG-0002 puts
model configuration under control-plane-owners. An admin-settable override would move
part of that decision outside CODEOWNERS review — so changing which model reviews the
agent's work is a control-plane PR, by design.
FIELDS
enabled  engines are crossed with reviewers, so N enabled engines cost N times as
much and produce N check runs per reviewer. One enabled = swap. Two =
cross-check.
model    null means 'let the engine pick its own default' — used where pinning a
specific model id would mean inventing one not verified to exist.
secret   name of the Actions secret holding this engine's credential. Read
generically as secrets[matrix.engine.secret]; never hardcoded in the core.
attribution  comment footer. Engine-specific on purpose: attributing a Codex review
to Claude Code would misstate which model produced the verdict.
requires_workflow_parity  true where the engine's own tooling refuses to run when
this workflow file differs from the default branch. That is
claude-code-action's anti-exfiltration rule (a PR must not be able to
rewrite the workflow AND obtain the app token), not a universal one — the
Codex CLI adapter uses a plain repository secret and has no such rule.
codex is shipped enabled:false. Its adapter is REAL, not a stub — written against the
verified `@openai/codex` CLI surface (`codex exec --model --sandbox -o`) — but it has
never executed end to end, because no CODEX_API_KEY is configured. Enabling it is a
config change plus a secret; treat its first run as unproven.
